title: "When a coroutine is deleted, the destructor of local variables (class instances) is not called."
body:
### Tested versions

Test version  godot  4.2 - 4.61

maybe 4.X all version



### System information

windows11 , CPU AMD Ryzen 7900 , RAM 48GB,   4060ti 16GB, dx12(vulcan) 

### Issue description

I created a manager that handles creating and deleting coroutines. However, when a coroutine is deleted while it is awaiting, the destructor of its local class instance variables is not called.

The destructor is only invoked if the coroutine itself explicitly returns from within its function.

Intuitively, deleting a coroutine should also clean up the local variables used inside it, and their destructors should be called. This behavior was natural when I coded with Lua scripts.

But in GDScript, unless the coroutine terminates itself, the destructors of local variables are not triggered.

I worked around this by using an if await return approach, but the more intuitive behavior would be that deleting a coroutine automatically cleans up its local variables and calls their destructors.

Even without my custom coroutine manager, it seems that in GDScript coroutines can be deleted at any time. So why does this bug exist?






### Steps to reproduce

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
example:
```gdscript
extends Node2D


class TestClass extends RefCounted:
	func _notification(what):
		if what == NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE:
			print("TestClass is end~? call check")
	
class MyCoroutine extends lpt.Coroutine:
	func run(arg,_myEnd := lpt.Coroutine._EndChecker.new(self)):
		var _test = TestClass.new()

		print(Time.get_ticks_msec() , " - start = id : "  + str(arg))
		if await co_wait_time(3): return 
		print(Time.get_ticks_msec() , " - do-1  = id : "  + str(arg)) 
		if await co_wait_time(3): return 
		print(Time.get_ticks_msec() , " - do-2  = id : "  + str(arg))
		if await co_wait_time(3): return 
		print(Time.get_ticks_msec() , " - end  = id : "  + str(arg))
		if await co_wait_time(1): return 
			
		print(Time.get_ticks_msec()," - co - end : " + str(arg))

	
func _ready():	

############################################################################################
###  When a coroutine is deleted from outside, local variable destructors are not called.
	var my_node = lpt.CoroutineMgr.__false_create( MyCoroutine.new(),"myarg")		
	await Engine.get_main_loop().create_timer(5).timeout
	lpt.CoroutineMgr.__false_erase(my_node)
#############################################################################################

####################################################################################
### Returns as a flag within the coroutine to induce termination , No Problem
	#var _co := lpt.CoroutineMgr.create( MyCoroutine.new(),"myarg")		
	#await Engine.get_main_loop().create_timer(5).timeout
	#_co.isDone = true
####################################################################################
	

	print("main end")
	
func _process(delta):
	lpt.CoroutineMgr.update(delta)
```
